In detail

Altstadt-Lehel is one of Munich's 25 official Stadtbezirke (city districts). Polizeipraesidium Muenchen and the Statistisches Amt Muenchen recorded 6,863 total offences here in 2025, across a population of 20,876 residents (31 December 2024) — a rate of 32,875 offences per 100,000 residents, roughly 6.6x the citywide Stadtbezirk average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central, station, or nightlife-heavy district can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential district can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. Altstadt-Lehel is Munich's historic centre — Marienplatz, the main shopping streets, and a dense concentration of hotels and restaurants sit here on a comparatively small resident base, so its rate reflects huge daytime and evening footfall against few registered residents rather than elevated risk per visit. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Munich — real Polizeipraesidium Muenchen / Statistisches Amt Muenchen figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Altstadt-Lehel safe?

Wandroz currently rates Altstadt-Lehel in Munich as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Munich. This rating is derived from Polizeipräsidium München's official recorded-offence statistics — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats. The source data has no day/night breakdown, so this single rating applies at any time of day rather than being a distinct night-specific figure.

Does Altstadt-Lehel's rating differ between day and night?

No — Altstadt-Lehel's source data has no time-of-day breakdown, so the same rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Munich) is shown for both day and night rather than Wandroz inventing a separate night figure it doesn't actually have.
